html:
Yaa Asantewaa was the queen mother of Ejisu in the Asante kingdom, in today's Ghana. In 1900 she led the Asante in a war against British rule, known as the War of the Golden Stool.

In 1896 the British had exiled the Asante king, Prempeh I, along with other leaders, among them Yaa Asantewaa's grandson. In 1900 the British governor demanded that the Asante hand over the Golden Stool, the sacred throne that held the soul of the nation, so he could sit on it. The chiefs met in secret. Yaa Asantewaa is remembered for shaming the men into action, saying that if they would not fight, the women would.

Asante forces besieged the British in their fort at Kumasi for months. Reinforcements broke the siege, and Yaa Asantewaa was captured in 1901 and exiled to the Seychelles, where she died. Asante was annexed to the Gold Coast colony in 1902. But the British never got the Golden Stool. She is a national heroine of independent Ghana.
